pattern: The approved architecture is a synthetic MedTech PMS pilot. Implementation approval does not authorize Azure deployment, real medical data or external transmissions.
implication: Prepare IaC only; default to private access and simulated transmissions. Require separate deployment and operational approval.

pattern: Initial planning had no inventory. Subsequent targeted read-only observations are privately bound to the reviewed original user, subscription and endpoints; no whole-tenant completeness, create permission or capacity guarantee follows.
implication: Keep identity and raw observation files private. Model catalog, quota and a single policy rule are separate from actual capacity, complete policy evaluation, deployment approval and a full cost estimate. Never invent resource IDs or reuse historical inventory as a current all-clear.

pattern: Model processing is EU-member-state-only. Current deployment-type docs include EFTA in the EU boundary while the privacy page uses EU-member-nations wording; neither DataZone nor a region label proves the requested boundary.
implication: Standard geography candidate only; no Global/DataZone/Developer fallback. AgentHost requires EU-Member-States and a canonical configuration-hash-bound review with actual processing countries. No legal/provider approval is inferred from hashing.

pattern: SQL is the authoritative business state with transactional audit/outbox/inbox; Blob stores evidence; Search is reconstructable. Durable uses separate Blob/Queue/Table storage and Operations is independent from agents.
implication: Separate identities and storage accounts, private endpoints and DNS for all three Durable services. Do not add a broker, AKS or Cosmos DB.

pattern: The allowed read-only application snapshot uses SDK 10.0.404 via global.json, Cohors.slnx, a React/Vite build and SQL integration tests requiring loopback COHORS_TEST_CONNECTION. The API serves static files and exposes /health/live and /health/ready.
implication: CI uses global.json, Node 24 LTS, the web lockfile and fresh real loopback SQL; no skipped suites are accepted. The infrastructure branch reads the existing bound primary application result rather than duplicating its tests. Confirmed target: cohors-api and separate cohors-agents on 8080, separate Flex code packages via OneDeploy. Cloud integration remains gated.

pattern: Four explicitly named enabled users were resolved by four exact read-only Graph GETs in the original bound context, with distinct identities. The user-specified alarm recipient is supplied through the existing private alertEmailReceivers input; it is not another bootstrap principal.

App roles, explicit product rights, the later Admin application contract and token/API readback remain separate. No test mail, delivery proof, 15-minute human acknowledgment, deputy or escalation is implied.

pattern: Consumption requires AzurePlatformDNS even with custom DNS; workload-profile environments alone are not Dedicated. Platform IP168.63.129.16 bypasses UDRs.
implication: Keep Consumption as the historical default, block its strict-DNS bootstrap and review explicit D4 plus both app assignments as a separate costed candidate. An owned NVA/resolver still needs mandatory platform-name resolution and separate ACA/Flex/operator end-to-end proofs; the successful Linux fixture does not establish these.

pattern: Medical-technical analysis, risk recommendations and assurance prioritize capability and measured quality. The dd112 source still supports exactly one shared Foundry profile, not role routing.
implication: Evaluate strong/frontier candidates against explicit version, EU-member-state boundary, allowed regional SKU, private access, capacity and task evidence. Do not select a cheap uniform default or infer clinical qualification from a model name. Evaluation provisioning and live-task authorization remain separate.

pattern: Production WORM duration, externally protected SQL ledger digests and recovery acceptance are not approved or live verified.
implication: Create separated storage boundaries without locking retention. Gate digest publishing, retention activation and restore acceptance explicitly; never open storage firewalls to make digest export work.

pattern: The coordinator read the original requirements matrix and mapped 118 unique IDs (104 mandatory, 14 recommended); the source-availability gap is closed, not the implementation or acceptance gaps. Architecture source is now v0.3.
implication: L-01 requires object-specific retention rather than blanket raw-data WORM; L-03 requires audit, recovery and independent digest evidence; L-05 preserves need-to-know, encryption, minimization and the separate Privacy/EU gate. Application documentation and individual acceptance remain with Cohors-Pilot.
